building.name: Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code, Part I, Virginia Construction Code
building.edition: 2021 (based on the 2021 International Building Code, with Virginia amendments)
building.local_amendments_note: Virginia's statewide code supersedes the building codes and regulations of cities (Code of Virginia § 36-98, re-read today), so Virginia Beach has no building or plumbing code amendments of its own. The city has no adopted-codes page with its own text: its Permits & Inspections page says the division 'administers the Uniform Statewide Building Code', and its Trades Permits and Commercial Building Permits pages link to the ICC's copies of the 2021 Virginia codes (codes.iccsafe.org/content/VACC2021P1 and VAPC2021P1; the ICC pages themselves were not read). The Virginia Beach City Code chapter on buildings (Municode) could not be read: Municode blocks automated access (HTTP 403).

fixtures.basis: Virginia's Uniform Statewide Building Code 'shall supersede the building codes and regulations of the counties, municipalities and other political subdivisions and state agencies' (Code of Virginia § 36-98, read today on law.lis.virginia.gov), so Virginia Beach cannot amend the toilet-count table or its rules. Nothing on Virginia Beach's permit pages changes the counts. The state pack's worked examples stand.

permit.exempt_list_quote: B. Section 108.2 Exemptions from application for permit. Notwithstanding the requirements of Section 108.1, application for a permit and any related inspections shall not be required for the following; however, this section shall not be construed to exempt such activities from other applicable requirements of this code. [...] 13. Construction work deemed by the building official to be minor and ordinary and that does not adversely affect public health or general safety. 14. Ordinary repairs that include the following: [...] 14.2. Replacement of plumbing fixtures and well pumps in all groups without alteration of the water supply and distribution systems, sanitary drainage systems, or vent systems. [...] 14.7. Installation or replacement of floor finishes in all occupancies. 14.8. Replacement of Class C interior wall or ceiling finishes installed in Groups A, E, and I and replacement of all classes of interior wall or ceiling finishes in other groups. 14.9. Installation or replacement of cabinetry or trim. 14.10. Application of paint or wallpaper. 14.11. Other repair work deemed by the building official to be minor and ordinary which does not adversely affect public health or general safety.
permit.required_quote: A. Section 108.1 When applications are required. Application for a permit shall be made to the building official and a permit shall be obtained prior to the commencement of any of the following activities [...] 1. Construction or demolition of a building or structure. Installations or alterations involving (i) the removal or addition of any wall, partition, or portion thereof; (ii) any structural component; (iii) the repair or replacement of any required component of a fire or smoke rated assembly; (iv) the alteration of any required means of egress system, including the addition or removal of emergency supplemental hardware; (v) water supply and distribution system, sanitary drainage system, or vent system; (vi) electric wiring; (vii) fire protection system, mechanical systems, or fuel supply systems; or (viii) any equipment regulated by the USBC.
permit.city_quote: A building permit is required to build or alter a commercial structure. [...] Construction or alteration of a commercial structure requiring permits include cutting away any wall, partition, or portion of the building; the removal or cutting of any structural beam; the removal or change of any required means of egress, or rearrangement of parts of the structure affecting the egress requirements.
permit.city_plumbing_quote: When is a plumbing permit required? [...] Commercial: New or replacement plumbing fixtures or drains / New or replacement testable backflow preventers / On-site water distribution or sewer collector lines / Replacement of water or sewer lines / Ultra-low flush toilet program. This list may not be applicable to, or inclusive of, all situations.
permit.note: The exempt list is the state's (13VAC5-63-80, Section 108.2 of the Virginia Construction Code), which applies in Virginia Beach; the city's pages publish no list of exempt work of their own, only lists of work that needs a permit. None of them names toilet partitions or toilet compartments. Section 108.1 and the city's page both require a permit for work on 'any wall, partition, or portion'; neither says whether a toilet stall partition is a 'partition' in that sense, and the question is not decided here. Whether the building official treats a like-for-like replacement as 'minor and ordinary' (items 13 and 14.11) is his decision. Note the city's plumbing FAQ lists 'new or replacement plumbing fixtures' in commercial buildings as needing a plumbing permit, while Section 108.2 item 14.2 exempts fixture replacement that leaves the piping alone; the page text therefore doesn't repeat the fixture exemption.
permit.office: City of Virginia Beach Permits & Inspections (Planning Department), Building 3, Municipal Center, 2403 Courthouse Drive

restrooms_city.note: No Virginia Beach ordinance on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms was found: one web search returned nothing for Virginia Beach beyond a city page stating its non-discrimination position (virginiabeach.gov/services/lgbtq-community-resources/leadership-legislation, seen in the search result only, not read), and the city's permit pages say nothing about restrooms. The Virginia Beach City Code itself (Municode) could not be read, so this is 'none found', not 'none exists'. Because the statewide building code supersedes local building regulations, the state rules in the state pack (single-user rooms marked for everyone; multi-user all-gender rooms allowed with floor-to-ceiling compartments) apply in Virginia Beach as written.

public_wage.state_law_note: Virginia has a prevailing wage law (§ 2.2-4321.3): mandatory for state agencies on public works over $250,000, and for a locality only if it adopts an ordinance. The Department of Labor and Industry publishes no rate table; its page says determinations 'are based on the applicable prevailing wage rate determinations made by the U.S. Secretary of Labor under the provisions of the Davis-Bacon Act', and the statute says the state rate may 'in no event' be lower than the Davis-Bacon rate. So the federal determination for Virginia Beach is the published figure, and the floor for a state determination.
public_wage.state_law_quote: "Prevailing wage rate" means the rate [...] as determined by the Commissioner on the basis of surveys conducted every three years, provided that (i) in no event shall the prevailing wage rate be lower than the prevailing wage rate determined by the U.S. Secretary of Labor under the provisions of the federal Davis-Bacon Act [...] C. Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, any locality may adopt an ordinance requiring that, when letting contracts for public works paid for in whole or in part by funds of the locality [...] N. The provisions of this section shall not apply to any public contract for public works of $250,000 or less.
public_wage.city_rule_note: Virginia Beach prevailing wage ordinance under § 2.2-4321.3 C: none found. Two web searches (ordinance and statute; council action 2025 or 2026) returned no Virginia Beach ordinance, agenda item or news report, while the same searches returned Richmond's (in effect July 1, 2025), Arlington's, Fairfax's and Prince William's. The city's Purchasing page and Supplier Services page (finance.virginiabeach.gov) contain no mention of a prevailing wage, Davis-Bacon or living wage requirement. The procurement chapter of the Virginia Beach City Code could not be read: Municode blocks automated access. This is 'none found', not 'confirmed none'. On the way, one search result (a news headline, not read) reported that a city budget raised the minimum wage for city employees to $15 an hour; that concerns city staff, not contractors. No living wage rule on city contracts was found.
public_wage.note: Modification 2 was the latest on sam.gov on 2026-11-24 (requests for modifications 3 to 6 returned 404). Found by reading the neighbouring determination numbers after Norfolk's (VA20260160): VA20260167 is the Building determination for the independent city of Virginia Beach.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Virginia Beach job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Virginia rules the city enforces.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Virginia Beach hotels, restaurants, offices and schools, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Virginia's statewide rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. A city can't change them, so Virginia Beach enforces them as the state writes them. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** the City of Virginia Beach's Permits & Inspections office issues building permits. The city requires one to alter a commercial building, including cutting away any wall or partition. Virginia's statewide rules exempt installing or replacing cabinetry or trim and work the building official considers minor and ordinary. Neither the city's page nor the state's lists name toilet partitions, so ask Permits & Inspections (757-385-4211) whether your replacement needs a permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of Virginia Beach's Permits & Inspections office
page.install_rule: Contractors, including carpentry businesses, pay a Virginia Beach license tax on gross receipts. Virginia requires a state contractor license for commercial jobs over $1,000: Class C covers single jobs up to $30,000, Class B up to $150,000, and Class A $150,000 and above. Virginia Beach asks for the contractor's Class A, B or C state registration number on a commercial building permit application. Confirm with the Virginia Beach Commissioner of the Revenue and the Virginia Board for Contractors. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: On a job over $1,000, the contractor needs a Virginia contractor license, and pays the Virginia Beach license tax on its receipts.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state agency projects over $250,000, Virginia law requires at least the prevailing wage set by the state's Commissioner of Labor and Industry, and a city, county or school division has to pay it only if it has passed its own ordinance. The state bases its rates on the federal ones and may not set them lower. The federal rate for a carpenter on building work in the City of Virginia Beach is $17.93 an hour plus $4.41 in benefits. For a City of Virginia Beach project, ask the city's Purchasing Division whether a wage requirement applies.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 6% in Virginia Beach: 4.3% state, 1% city and a 0.7% regional tax that applies across Hampton Roads.
page.buyers_extra: - **Oceanfront hotels and beach facilities:** solid plastic or phenolic with stainless steel hardware, for restrooms that see salt air, sand and wet floors.
sources: - Codes enforced in Virginia Beach: the statewide code applies in every Virginia city (see the state sources below); the city enforces it through the Permits & Inspections Division of its Planning Department, 2403 Courthouse Drive: City of Virginia Beach, [Permits & Inspections](https://planning.virginiabeach.gov/divisions-offices/permits-inspections), [Commercial Building Permits](https://planning.virginiabeach.gov/permits/building/commercial-building-permits) and [Trades Permits](https://planning.virginiabeach.gov/permits/trade). Checked 2026-11-24.

- When a permit is needed and what is exempt: [13VAC5-63-80, Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code, Section 108, Application for permit](https://law.lis.virginia.gov/admincode/title13/agency5/chapter63/section80/) (Section 108.1, work that needs a permit; Section 108.2, exemptions), and the City of Virginia Beach's [Commercial Building Permits](https://planning.virginiabeach.gov/permits/building/commercial-building-permits) page ("Construction or alteration of a commercial structure requiring permits", phone 757-385-4211). Neither names toilet partitions. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax in Virginia Beach: Virginia Tax, [Sales and Use Tax](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/sales-and-use-tax) (6% in Hampton Roads, Virginia Beach listed) and its [Sales Tax Rates by Locality](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/sites/default/files/inline-files/sales-and-use-tax-rates-by-locality-by-date.xlsx) spreadsheet (Virginia Beach 6% since July 1, 2013); the parts are in the Code of Virginia sections listed under Sales tax below. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Carpenter rate on federally funded building work in the City of Virginia Beach: [federal wage determination VA20260167, modification 2, May 18, 2026](https://sam.gov/wage-determination/VA20260167/2). State rates are based on the federal ones and may not be lower: [Code of Virginia § 2.2-4321.3](https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title2.2/chapter43/section2.2-4321.3/) and [Virginia Department of Labor and Industry, Prevailing Wage Law](https://doli.virginia.gov/labor-law/prevailing-wage-law/). City contracts: City of Virginia Beach, [Purchasing](https://finance.virginiabeach.gov/purchasing). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Contractor registration number on the permit application: City of Virginia Beach, [Commercial Building Permits](https://planning.virginiabeach.gov/permits/building/commercial-building-permits) ("general contractor's Class A, B or C state registration number") and the [Application for Commercial New/Addition/Alteration Permit](https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/virginia-beach-departments-docs/planning/Divisions-Offices/Permits_Inspections/Documents/Commercial-Permit-Application.pdf); business license issued by the Commissioner of the Revenue: [Business Taxpayers](https://cor.virginiabeach.gov/businesses/business-taxpayers). Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; ICC A117.1-2017 as referenced by the 2021 Virginia Construction Code; 2021 Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code, Part I, Virginia Construction Code (2021 International Building Code with Virginia amendments, 13VAC5-63), in force since January 18, 2024, enforced in Virginia Beach by the Permits & Inspections Division of the Planning Department without local amendments (Code of Virginia § 36-98); 2021 Virginia Plumbing Code (2021 International Plumbing Code with Virginia amendments); Section 108 of the Virginia Construction Code (13VAC5-63-80) for permits; NFPA 286 for HDPE.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether replacing or adding toilet partitions in an existing commercial restroom needs a Virginia Beach building permit, and whether the building official reads 'any wall, partition, or portion' to include toilet stall partitions (Permits & Inspections, 757-385-4211, perminsp@vbgov.com).

Virginia Beach prevailing wage ordinance: none found in two web searches or on the city's Purchasing and Supplier Services pages; the City Code's procurement chapter (on Municode) could not be read. The page therefore doesn't say Virginia Beach has none: it tells the buyer to ask the Purchasing Division (757-385-4438). Confirm in a browser or by phone, then say it outright.

The Virginia Beach City Code (Municode) blocks automated access: no check of the code itself for a restroom sign rule, a wage rule or the buildings chapter. A browser check of the code for 'restroom', 'toilet' and 'prevailing wage' closes all three.
Virginia Beach's website has no adopted-codes text of its own: its permit pages link to the ICC's copies of the 2021 Virginia codes. The edition and date are the state's (DHCD).

The city's plumbing FAQ lists 'new or replacement plumbing fixtures' in commercial buildings as needing a plumbing permit, while the state's exempt list covers fixture replacement that leaves the piping alone; the permit bullet leaves fixtures out for that reason.
The carpenter rate in the federal determination is a 2016 survey rate (SUVA2013-052) and sits below the metro median wage shown in the bullet above it.
The four building types in the lead and the buyers bullet on oceanfront hotels and beach facilities are editorial, not sourced.

The contractor sentence ('pay a Virginia Beach license tax on gross receipts') is the local-rules entry as written (City Code § 18-75, read in part in a browser on 2026-11-03, medium confidence); the Commissioner of the Revenue's Business Taxpayers page read today confirms only that the office issues business licenses.

The federal wage determination's class is 'Carpenter, includes acoustical ceiling installation, drywall hanging, and form work'; whether partition installers are classed as carpenters on a given job is the contracting agency's call.
